Einsteinium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Es and atomic number 99 and is a member of the actinide series and the seventh transuranium element.
In what year was Jean Tatlock born?
Jean Tatlock: Jean Frances Tatlock (February 21, 1914 – January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
In what year did Nikola Tesla die?
Nikola Tesla (10 July 1856 – 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American engineer, futurist, and inventor.
In what year was Chlorine discovered?
Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
Mikoyan MiG-35: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. Marketed as a 4++ generation jet fighter, it is a further development of the MiG-29M/M2 and MiG-29K/KUB fighters.
In which country is Fish and chips?
Fish and chips: United Kingdom. Fish and chips is a hot dish consisting of battered and fried fish, served with chips.
Who is credited with discovering Rhodium?
Rhodium: William Hyde Wollaston. Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
Who is credited with discovering Ibuprofen?
Ibuprofen: Stewart Adams. Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that is used to relieve pain, fever, and inflammation.
Who is credited with discovering Carbon?
Carbon: Antoine Lavoisier. Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
Drugs that meddle with this neurotransmitter can do everything from paralyze to cause convulsions, since it's the signal motor neurons use to activate muscles. What is it?
Acetylcholine (ACh) is an organic compound that functions in the brain and body of many types of animals (including humans) as a neurotransmitter.
With one stable isotope and the rank of 12th-most-abundant element in the universe, this lightweight metal carries atomic number 13 — what is it?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
It can't touch a virus or a fungus, but a few varieties even fight protozoa — this class of drug is the frontline weapon against bacterial infection; what is it?
Antibiotic is a type of antimicrobial substance active against bacteria.

Driven mainly by elevated LDL cholesterol, this chronic inflammatory disease quietly builds plaque-filled lesions in artery walls until, often by middle age, it can trigger a stroke or heart trouble — what is it?
Atherosclerosis is a pattern of the disease arteriosclerosis, characterized by development of abnormalities called lesions in walls of arteries.
Usually the tenth-brightest star in the night sky, this red supergiant in the constellation Orion varies noticeably in brightness over a roughly 400-day cycle — name the star?
Betelgeuse is a red supergiant star in the equatorial constellation of Orion. Its Bayer designation is α Orionis, Latinised to Alpha Orionis and abbreviated Alpha Ori or α Ori.
Despite being fully Turing-complete, this minimalist 1993 esoteric language allows only eight commands and takes its unusual name from a slang term for utter confusion — what language is it?
Brainfuck is an esoteric programming language created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Mller.
This biological family includes domestic dogs, wolves, coyotes, foxes, and jackals, found on every continent except Antarctica. What family is it?
Canidae (from Latin, canis, "dog") is a biological family of caniform carnivorans, constituting a clade.
Which American political scientist drew fierce controversy as co-author of the 1994 book 'The Bell Curve' and author of the welfare-system critique 'Losing Ground'?
Charles Murray (political scientist) (born January 8, 1943) is an American political scientist.
Its glorious blue in glass and paint was long wrongly blamed on bismuth, and frustrated miners named its ore after a goblin. Which hard, gray element carries the symbol Co?
Cobalt is a chemical element; it has symbol Co and atomic number 27.
Tolerant of poor, sandy soil, this legume was domesticated in Africa millennia ago and is now grown far more in Nigeria and Niger than anywhere else on Earth — which crop?
Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.
When insulin runs short, the body burns fat into acidic ketones, causing deep gasping breaths and fruity-smelling breath in this potentially life-threatening emergency — what is it?
Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a potentially life-threatening acute complication of diabetes mellitus.
Trained in both mathematics and philosophy, which Austrian-German thinker developed the concept of phenomenological reduction and founded a major 20th-century school of philosophy?
Edmund Husserl (Austrian; 8 April 1859 - 27 April 1938) was an Austrian-German philosopher and mathematician who established the school of phenomenology.
This class of chemical compounds forms when the hydrogen of an acid's hydroxyl group is replaced by a carbon-based group, and includes the fatty-acid derivatives called glycerides. What is it?
Ester is a compound derived from an acid (either organic or inorganic) in which the hydrogen atom (H) of at least one acidic hydroxyl group (OH) of that acid is replaced by an organyl group (R).

With over 2,400 described species, these soft-bodied beetles produce light mainly at twilight, an ability that likely began as a larval warning signal before evolving into an adult mating display. Name this insect family?
Firefly are a family of elateroid beetles with more than 2,400 described species, many of which are light-emitting.
Its name comes from Greek words meaning "study of the earth," and this science examines the rocks and processes that shape not just our planet but other astronomical bodies too — what field is it?
Geology is a branch of natural science concerned with the Earth and other astronomical bodies, the rocks of which they are composed, and the processes by which they change over time.

This German physicist turned his eye on the mind itself, founding psychophysics and giving his name to a law showing that sensation rises with the logarithm — not the raw intensity — of a stimulus. Whose pioneering work was it?
Gustav Fechner (19 April 1801 - 18 November 1887) was a German physicist, philosopher, and experimental psychologist.
Sometimes called urticaria, this itchy rash of raised welts can flare for minutes or days, may follow an allergy or infection, and in half of all cases has no identifiable cause — what is it?
Hives is a kind of skin rash with red or flesh-colored, raised, itchy bumps.
First used ritually by forager tribes in Central Africa and later adopted by Gabon's Bwiti tradition, this psychoactive plant alkaloid interacts with both opioid and serotonin receptors — what is it?
Ibogaine is a psychoactive indole alkaloid derived from plants such as Tabernanthe iboga, characterized by hallucinogenic and oneirogenic effects.
The first woman ever to chair the Federal Reserve, she later became the first woman to serve as U.S. Treasury secretary — a Brooklyn-born, Yale-trained economist. Who is she?
Janet Yellen (born August 13, 1946) is an American economist who served as the 78th United States secretary of the treasury from 2021 to 2025 and as chair of the Federal Reserve from 2014 to 2018.
Born in 1972, this Canadian atmospheric scientist holds an endowed public-policy chair at Texas Tech and in 2021 became Chief Scientist at the Nature Conservancy — who is she?
Katharine Hayhoe (born 1972) is a Canadian atmospheric scientist.
This Swiss polymath founded the study of graph theory and topology, and introduced much of modern mathematical notation, including the concept of a function — who is he?
Leonhard Euler (15 April 1707 - 18 September 1783) was a Swiss polymath who was active as a mathematician, physicist, astronomer, logician, geographer, music theorist and engineer.
Named for their strong, monogamous pair bonding and the long stretches paired birds spend sitting together, this small genus of African parrots is popular as a pet — what is it commonly called?
Lovebird is the common name for the genus Agapornis, a small group of parrots in the Old World parrot family Psittaculidae.
Covering everything from B2B deals to a government's 'Got Milk?'-style campaigns, this business pillar means acquiring, satisfying and retaining customers — what is this discipline called?
Marketing is the act of acquiring, satisfying and retaining customers. It is one of the primary components of business management and commerce.
This Hungarian-American psychologist identified and named the highly focused, creativity-boosting mental state known as 'flow' — who is he?
Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi (29 September 1934 - 20 October 2021) was a Hungarian-American psychologist.
Caused by antibodies blocking acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, this autoimmune disease most often weakens the muscles of the eyes, face and throat — which disease?
Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a long-term neuromuscular junction disease that leads to varying degrees of skeletal muscle weakness.
A child prodigy turned MIT mathematician, this American thinker is considered the originator of cybernetics — the science of communication in living things and machines. Who was he?
Norbert Wiener (November 26, 1894 - March 18, 1964) was an American computer scientist, mathematician, and philosopher.
Often linked to polycystic ovary syndrome or pelvic inflammatory disease, this fluid-filled sac can cause severe pain if it ruptures or twists — what is it?
Ovarian cyst is a fluid-filled sac within the ovary. If the cyst either breaks open or causes twisting of the ovary, it may cause severe pain.
This aromatic herb is a natural hybrid between watermint and spearmint, native to Europe and the Middle East but now cultivated worldwide — what plant is it?
Peppermint (Mentha piperita) is a hybrid species of mint, a cross between watermint and spearmint.
This GABA-derived drug treats cognitive disorders, vertigo, and dyslexia, and shares its 'racetam' drug class with related compounds like levetiracetam and aniracetam — what is it?
Piracetam is a drug that has efficacy in cognitive disorders, vertigo, cortical myoclonus, dyslexia, and sickle cell anemia; sources differ on its usefulness for dementia.

This mammal genus includes a familiar, masked, ring-tailed nocturnal visitor common across North America, plus two lesser-known tropical relatives; its closest kin are the ring-tailed cats and cacomistles. What animal is this?
Procyon (genus) is a genus of nocturnal mammals comprising three species commonly known as raccoons in the family Procyonidae.
A medium-sized tropical tree native to Southeast Asia, it's a close relative of the lychee and longan and shares its name with the edible fruit it bears — what is it?
Rambutan (Nephelium lappaceum) is a medium-sized tropical tree in the family Sapindaceae.
Native to West Africa and later naturalized across Asia and the West Indies, this plant's stems yield fibre while its calyces are steeped for a popular infusion — what is it?
Roselle (plant) (Sabdariffa gossypiifolia) is a species of flowering plant in the genus Sabdariffa that is native to Africa, most likely West Africa.
First described in 1779, which large African raptor stands over four feet tall on stilt-like legs and is grouped in its own family, Sagittariidae?
Secretarybird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a large bird of prey that is endemic to Africa.
With symbol Na from the Neo-Latin 'natrium' and a single stable isotope, this reactive metal sits in group 1 and is found in minerals like halite and feldspar — what is it?
Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.

This medical emergency occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is blocked or reduced, causing cell death — its warning signs include facial drooping and sudden difficulty speaking or moving one side of the body. Name the condition?

Stroke is a medical condition in which blood flow to a part of the brain is reduced or blocked causing cell death. There are two main types of stroke: ischemic, due to lack of blood flow, and hemorrhagic, due to bleeding.
Caused by Clostridium tetani, this infection brings on recurring muscle spasms that can last weeks and prove fatal in about 10% of cases — what is it commonly known as?
Tetanus (from Ancient Greek 'tension', 'stretched', 'rigid'), also known as lockjaw, is a bacterial infection caused by Clostridium tetani and characterized by muscle spasms.
When water loss to the air outpaces uptake by the roots, plants shut tiny leaf pores to conserve moisture, slowing this evaporative water-movement process — what's it called?
Transpiration is the process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts, such as leaves, stems and flowers.
Native only to the wetlands of the Carolinas, which carnivorous plant snaps shut a 'jaw' formed from the tips of its leaves when an insect trips it?
Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula) is a carnivorous plant native to the temperate and subtropical wetlands of North Carolina and South Carolina, on the East Coast of the United States.
Common across Europe and also found in Asia, this large carpenter bee bores its nest into dead wood rather than building a hive — which species?
Xylocopa violacea is the common European species of carpenter bee, and one of the largest bees in Europe.
Genetic in roughly 80% of cases, this long-term skin condition clogs hair follicles with dead skin and sebum, producing blackheads and pimples on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne: Skin condition characterized by pimples.

German-born theoretical physicist celebrated for E=mc² and work on relativity — he won the 1921 Nobel Prize not for those breakthroughs, but for discovering the photoelectric effect. Who revolutionized physics across multiple domains?
Named for its males' mating call, which sounds like a farm animal bellowing, this large amphibian native to eastern North America has been introduced worldwide as a food source — which species?
American bullfrog: Species of amphibian. It typically inhabits large permanent water bodies such as swamps, ponds, and lakes.
Belonging to the suborder Vermilingua and closely related to sloths, these mammals include giant, silky, and tamandua species that feed almost exclusively on ants and termites — what are they called?
Anteater: Mammals known for eating ants and termites.
Native to eastern North America's wet woods and swamps, this shrub genus produces bitter 'chokeberries' that reached Scandinavia and Russia by the eighteenth century — what genus is this?

Aronia: Genus of plants (chokeberries). Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
This Mexican mole salamander never grows up — it reaches sexual maturity while staying fully aquatic with feathery external gills, skipping metamorphosis entirely. What is it?
Axolotl: Species of salamander. The axolotl (from Classical Nahuatl: āxōlōtl [aːˈʃoːloːtɬ]; Ambystoma mexicanum) is a species of mole salamander.
Named after the aromatic resin from which it was first derived, this simplest aromatic carboxylic compound forms salts widely used as food preservatives — what is it called?

Native to North America and classified in the genus Vaccinium, this fruit comes in wild 'lowbush' and cultivated 'highbush' varieties, with Canada leading global production of the wild type — what fruit is it?
Blueberry: Perennial plant with blue berries.
Known for a widely viewed 2010 TEDx talk on shame and vulnerability, which academic wrote six consecutive number-one New York Times bestsellers, including Daring Greatly?
Brené Brown: American academic, speaker and author.
This highly soluble white crystalline salt is spread on icy roads for de-icing and, in its anhydrous form, works as a moisture-absorbing desiccant. What compound is it?
Calcium chloride: Chemical compound. The compound is a white crystalline solid at room temperature, and it is highly soluble in water.
Native to the Mediterranean, this legume tree's seed pods are ground into a chocolate substitute, while its seeds yield a common food thickener known as locust bean gum — which tree?
Carob: Small tree grown for its edible pods and landscaping.
This goat-antelope roams mountain ranges from the Pyrenees to the Caucasus and has even been introduced to New Zealand's South Island — which animal?
In this chronic liver condition, healthy tissue is replaced by scar tissue and regenerative nodules, choking blood flow and causing portal hypertension — what is it called?
Cirrhosis: Chronic disease of the liver, characterized by fibrosis.
In mathematics, this is a selection of items from a set where the order of choosing them does not matter, unlike a permutation — what is it called?

Combination: Selection of items from a set. In mathematics, a combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).
Domesticated in Africa and thriving in sandy, low-rainfall soil, this ancient legume is now grown mostly in Nigeria and Niger, which together supply two-thirds of the world's crop — which plant?
Cowpea: Species of plant. The cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.
Son of a bass-baritone and born into a family of engineers, this American built his first car at 19, won four F1 Grands Prix, and took Le Mans in 1967 — who was he?
Dan Gurney: American racing driver, engineer and motorsport executive (1931–2018)
This colorless, highly flammable liquid with a sweet smell was once widely used as a general anesthetic before modern alternatives — what compound?
Defined in humans as an adult height of four foot ten or shorter, this condition's most common form — accounting for about 70% of cases — is a genetic disorder called achondroplasia. What is it?
Dwarfism: Small size of an organism, caused by growth deficiency or genetic mutations.
This Italian-American physicist discovered two elements, technetium and astatine, plus the antiproton — the last earning him a share of the 1959 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was he?
Emilio Segrè: Italian-American nuclear physicist and radiochemist (1905–1989)
Marketed under brand names like Arcoxia, this selective COX-2 inhibitor developed by Merck was approved in 63 countries by 2007 — everywhere, notably, except the United States — what is the drug?
This membranous bodily structure comes in superficial, visceral, and deep types, and a dangerous pressure buildup within it can cause compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Fascia: Layer of connective tissue in the body.

Members of this insect order have just one pair of true wings — the hindwings evolved into balance organs called halteres — and the group includes mosquitoes among its 150,000+ species. What are they commonly called?
Fly: Order of insects. A fly (pl. flies) is an insect of the order Diptera (from Ancient Greek δι- di- 'two' and πτερόν pteron 'wing'), named for the single pair of wings.
Caused by a loss of blood supply and marked by skin turning red or black, this condition comes in dry, wet, and gas forms — what is it?
Gangrene: Type of tissue death by ischemia.

Inducted into the U.S. Air Force Hall of Fame in 2018, this American mathematician modeled the precise shape of the Earth — work later baked into the Global Positioning System that now guides your phone. Who is she?
With long, whip-like antennae and a global range except Antarctica, this insect family — known as true crickets — includes burrowing giants that dig meter-deep tunnels. What is the family called?
Gryllidae: Family of crickets. The family Gryllidae contains the subfamilies and genera which entomologists now term true crickets.

Formally described only in 1983, this helical, flagella-driven bacterium burrows through the stomach's mucous lining and is the chief culprit behind gastric ulcers and some stomach cancers. What is it?
Nicknamed 'Hobbit,' this extinct species of small archaic humans stood about 1.1 meters tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago — which species?
Homo floresiensis: Extinct small human species found in Flores.

Typically begun with an induction of preliminary instructions, this state of focused attention and heightened suggestibility is debated as either an altered trance or a form of imaginative role-play — what is it?
Hypnosis: State of increased suggestibility. There are competing theories explaining hypnosis and related phenomena.
This cerebrovascular condition is a localized ballooning of a brain blood vessel most often found in the Circle of Willis, with the 'berry'-shaped type being the most common. What is it?

Intracranial aneurysm: Ballooning or rupturing of a blood vessel in the brain. The risk of rupture varies with the size and location of the aneurysm, with those in the posterior circulation being more prone to rupture.
After a cross-country road trip from New York to Seattle, this Princeton engineering graduate founded an online bookstore in 1994 that grew into a global e-commerce giant. Who is he?
This twin-engine fighter jet program made its home nation the fourth in the world to develop stealth avionics, joining the ranks of the US, China, and Russia — which aircraft?
KAI KF-21 Boramae: South Korean fighter aircraft.
Born of Peranakan Chinese cuisine, this spicy Southeast Asian noodle dish is often served in a rich coconut-curry soup soured with tamarind — what is it?
Laksa: Spicy noodle dish from Southeast Asia.
This genus of bulb-grown flowering plants, prized for their large blooms, is highly toxic to cats — even though many unrelated plants borrow its common name — which genus?
Lilium: Genus of plants. Lilium ( LIL-ee-əm) is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants growing from bulbs, all with large and often prominent flowers.
This best-known stag beetle species in Western Europe lends its genus its very name, and is currently listed as Near Threatened — what is it?
Lucanus cervus: Species of beetle. L. cervus is listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN Red List.

One of the most colorful mammals alive, this West African monkey sports vivid red-and-blue facial skin and lives in huge groups called 'hordes' — though long mistaken for a baboon, it's actually closer kin to mangabeys. What is it?
Mandrill: Species of Old World monkey from Africa.

Co-inventor of a heart-valve repair device called the MitraClip, this Turkish-American cardiac surgeon became a famous TV health personality before being named the 17th administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services in 2025 — who is he?
Mehmet Oz: American TV host and government official (born 1960)
Often striking one side of the head and sometimes preceded by a sensory 'aura,' this neurological disorder brings nausea and sensitivity to light and sound — what is it?
Migraine: Disorder resulting in recurrent moderate–severe headaches.
Named for its rough alignment with the Moon's cycle — the two words are even linguistic cognates — this calendar unit varies from 28 to 31 days in the Gregorian system — what is it?
Month: Unit of time, usually 28 to 31 days.
The only mammal that's essentially cold-blooded, this burrowing "sand puppy" of the Horn of Africa also lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen — what creature is it?
This reddish-brown, poisonous gas (formula NO2) is a key step in making nitric acid for fertilizer — and your gas stove quietly produces it while you cook. What is it?

A subdiscipline of metaphysics, this philosophical study of being asks what reality's most general features are, sorting things into particulars like Socrates and universals like the color green — what is it?
Ontology: Philosophical study of being. For example, social ontology examines basic concepts used in the social sciences.
This cat-family genus contains the five biggest living cats — jaguar, leopard, lion, snow leopard, and tiger — plus extinct relatives like the cave lion and American lion. Which genus is it?
A hybrid cross of watermint and spearmint, this herb is one of the oldest used in cooking and medicine and a key plant source of menthol — what is it?
Peppermint: Hybrid flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae.

For two thousand years it lived inside natural philosophy alongside chemistry and biology, only breaking off as its own discipline during the 17th-century Scientific Revolution; what is this study of matter, energy, and force?
Physics: Scientific field of study. It is one of the most fundamental scientific disciplines.
First domesticated some 5,000 years ago on the Iranian plateau, this fruit-bearing shrub reached California in 1769 via Spanish settlers — which fruit?
Pomegranate: Fruit-bearing deciduous shrub. Pomegranate was first domesticated by ancient Iranians in the Iranian plateau and nearby regions about 5,000 years ago.
Created in the early 18th century, this dark pigment was the first modern synthetic color, made by oxidizing iron ferrocyanide salts — what is it?
Prussian blue: Synthetic pigment. Prussian blue (also known as Berlin blue, Brandenburg blue, Parisian and Paris blue) is a dark blue pigment produced by oxidation of ferrous ferrocyanide salts.
Element 88 reacts with nitrogen rather than oxygen in air, turning black, and once glowed in self-luminous paints despite being highly carcinogenic — which element is it?
Radium: Chemical element with atomic number 88 (Ra)
Curving around the chest, these bones protect the lungs and heart and, in snakes, support and protect the whole body — what are they called?
Rib: Long bone in vertebrates that protects vital respiratory and cardiovascular organs.
Originally conceived as a jet trainer before its role expanded to supersonic strike and reconnaissance, this Anglo-French attack aircraft is today flown only by the Indian Air Force. What is it?
SEPECAT Jaguar: French/British attack aircraft. It was also later license produced by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited in India for use of the Indian Air Force.

Originally from the Mediterranean, this yellowish-gray arthropod has up to 15 pairs of long legs and preys on insects with venom too mild to harm humans — what species commonly invades homes worldwide?
Scutigera coleoptrata: Species of arthropod. Scutigera coleoptrata, also known as the house centipede, is a species of centipede that is typically yellowish-gray and has up to 15 pairs of long legs.
Better known by the brand name Viagra, this drug treats erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension, kicking in within about twenty minutes — what is it?

Sildenafil: Drug for erectile dysfunction and hypertension. Sildenafil, sold under the brand name Viagra among others, is a medication used to treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Commonly grown as an easy-care houseplant that tolerates low light, this genus of about 60 tropical species is better known by the nickname 'peace lily' — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum: Genus of plants. Certain species of Spathiphyllum are commonly known as spath or peace lilies.
Usually found in pairs and recognized as a leading cause of pneumonia since the late 19th century, which bacterium often lives harmlessly in the respiratory tracts of healthy carriers?
Streptococcus pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Streptococcus pneumoniae, or pneumococcus, is a Gram-positive, spherical bacteria, alpha-hemolytic member of the genus Streptococcus.
This orange citrus fruit is usually considered a mandarin variety, though it's also thought to carry some pomelo ancestry — which fruit?
One of the three great clades of dinosaur, its members share hollow bones and three clawed toes per limb, were ancestrally carnivorous, and likely wore feathers in the Coelurosauria — which group?
Linked to the use of highly absorbent tampons, this bacterial-toxin condition causes fever, rash, skin peeling, and a dangerous drop in blood pressure — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome: Medical condition caused by bacterial toxins.
One of the two main inflammatory bowel diseases, this long-term condition inflames and ulcerates the colon and rectum, causing abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea — what is it?
Ulcerative colitis: Inflammatory bowel disease that causes ulcers in the colon.
This Russian-Canadian programmer co-founded Bitcoin Magazine in 2011 before deploying a rival blockchain platform in 2015 alongside Gavin Wood and Charles Hoskinson — who is he?
Ranging from a few meters for Bluetooth to millions of kilometers for deep-space signals, this method of sending information relies on radio waves instead of cables -- what is it called?
Wireless: Transfer of information or power that does not require the use of physical wires.
Tellurium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for tellurium is Te. Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
Darmstadtium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for darmstadtium is Ds. Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.

Paul Newman: Paul Leonard Newman (January 26, 1925 – September 26, 2008) was an American actor, filmmaker, racecar driver, philanthropist, and entrepreneur.
